description.en: Implements a single feature in a generated SaaS app: snippet-apply, agentic code-gen, factory test, optional auto-fix, code-review. Requires a SaaS factory in the project (directory saas-factory/ or FACTORY_ROOT with the CLI tools/factory); it is not part of this repository.
description.de: Implementiert ein einzelnes Feature: snippet-apply, agentic Code-Gen, factory test, optional Auto-Fix, Code-Review. Voraussetzung: eine SaaS-Factory im Projekt (Verzeichnis saas-factory/ oder FACTORY_ROOT mit der CLI tools/factory); sie gehört nicht zu diesem Repository.

author: MySuricates
instructions: Implements exactly ONE feature in the target project. Hard rule: NEVER claim success without a green factory test. Fix tests instead of hiding them. Never invent libraries — if something is missing, extend package.json.

config.command:
set -euo pipefail
FACTORY="${FACTORY_ROOT:-./saas-factory}"
SLUG="{{ slug }}"
FEATURE_ID="{{ feature_id }}"
STACK="{{ stack }}"
TARGET="$FACTORY/$SLUG"
"$FACTORY/tools/factory" snippet-apply --feature "$FEATURE_ID" --stack "$STACK" --target "$TARGET" 2>&1 || echo 'No snippet available — the agentic block generates from scratch'

config.success_criteria: factory test in the project directory returns JSON with ok=true (lint/typecheck/unit all passed).
config.goal:
Implement the feature {{ feature_id }} in project {{ slug }}.

CONTEXT:
- Project path: ${FACTORY_ROOT:-./saas-factory}/{{ slug }}
- Feature description: {{ feature_desc }}
- Stack: {{ stack }}
- Snippet result (block 1 above): {{ previous_output }}

TASK:
1. If the snippet already copied files, fill the gaps (TODO markers, missing imports, business logic).
2. Otherwise: generate all files for the feature from scratch, in the stack-specific idiom (Next.js App Router → src/app/, server actions in src/lib/, Prisma schema extensions in prisma/schema.prisma).
3. Write at least one unit test (Vitest/Jest/pytest depending on the stack).
4. If the Prisma schema changes: adjust ONLY the schema file — the migration runs afterwards via `factory migrate`.
5. Briefly update README.md (1-2 sentences for the new feature).
6. Iterate via factory test (run it in the project directory) until ok=true.

Use ABSOLUTE PATHS — every ACTION is its own agent without the context of the previous ones.
No incremental refactors outside the feature.
Do not hard-code secrets — maintain .env.example.

If factory test fails: read log_tail in the JSON report, fix it in a targeted way, re-run. Never disable or skip tests.

config.command:
set -euo pipefail
FACTORY="${FACTORY_ROOT:-./saas-factory}"
SLUG="{{ slug }}"
TARGET="$FACTORY/$SLUG"
RESULT=$("$FACTORY/tools/factory" test "$TARGET")
echo "$RESULT"
OK=$(echo "$RESULT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d["ok"])')
if [ "$OK" != "True" ] && [ "$OK" != "true" ]; then
  echo 'TEST_FAILED'
  "$FACTORY/tools/factory" create-todo "feature {{ feature_id }} in {{ slug }} — tests failed" --tag test-failed --tag {{ slug }} --tag {{ feature_id }} --priority HIGH --workflow-run "{{ workflow_run_id }}" --reference-type 'feature_test_failure' --reference-id '{{ feature_id }}' >&2 || true
else
  echo 'TEST_OK'
fi

You are a code reviewer. Review the changes for feature {{ feature_id }} in project {{ slug }}.

Project path: ${FACTORY_ROOT:-./saas-factory}/{{ slug }}

TASK:
1. Look at the last commit (`cd $PROJEKT && git log -1 --stat && git show HEAD`)
2. Assess: bugs, security issues, performance, maintainability
3. Output ONLY findings with severity HIGH or CRITICAL — no style nitpicking
4. If everything is OK: 'CODE_REVIEW: PASSED — no findings'
5. If there are findings: a list with File:Line + description + suggested fix
